### 2026-10-06 – October 6:

**2.5h**

October 6:
I originally set out to just start the project for today, but I had a few goals in mind after wrapping my head around what I really needed to do.

 - figure out what I wanted to build and post a video on it: originally, I tried to use TinkerCad, but that proved a little too time-consuming, so I built a 2d version in Miro instead.

![2D Miro video](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/2dd18114262241d32cb1f23472828c23e491fb462fcaad6d0cdfed4088754515.png)

![scrapped 3d model](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/0a2a646749e0c0804339df1dda0d997865e3ea3e225083fc0a8930e67ab87f85.png)

 - get my repo check done, I used claude code for the majority of this (more on this later!), specifically the PCD on KiCad and the firmware. But after revising the docs, I realized that it wasn't faithful to the terms and values of half-life. And next session, I'll go back, delete everything, and only use the previously generated work as a guide while doing it ALL MYSELF!

 - Things for set up I did do, setting up hackatime was challenging for me, for some reason, I was only seeing other... on the list dropdown, but after using Claude PROPERLY, finagling with GitHub repos and local repos, it all worked out and I could finally track my code hours

![I couldn't see anything past the pesky other..., but now maybe I see too much?](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/ac10ddbdba8ae42f029c4aef1000bec364df1b1ebc03c14147069ec26aa2dc03.png)

 -  next session, I'll redo everything with proper guidance and work, and I'll finish the goals I originally set out to do ( finishing the GitHub checklist)

tldr: Learned all about the half-life process and how the program works. Learned the hard way to always check doc rules appropriately and use Claude Code appropriately, as a tool. Learned to work efficiently and focus on one task at a time.

### 2026-10-08 – October 8:

**3h**

October 8:
In the previous session, I wanted to start on the things that Claude Code had done for me before, but it became immediately clear that I had to finish the component list first. So, today I planned to finish the BOM file, getting all my components and parts down for my device. I didn't realize it would be so hard, though. I truly thought it would be a 1-hour task max.

1. I had a first iteration of the parts list. I thought it would be the last one, so I didn't take a screenshot. It was mostly full of negative things, but it was a great learning experience:
 - I didn't realize how interconnected devices were; it didn't have wiring, insulation, and the battery pack was quite simplistic
 - It really didn't follow my original plan. I had an external battery, an overkill motor, and components of wildly different sizes.
 - At this point, my budget was looking great, sitting at ~$40.

![1st+2nd list iteration](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/8a41e68aaddc04d6a3f72590db450ffaa3b8d762226357c086dc86cc75f39e80.png)

2. My next iteration was extremely different. I realized how many issues my original list/plan had, and I had to change many components entirely. During the process, I also learned more about how my device would work, and it changed my original design and view of what it should look like. Of course, I still ran into many issues.
 - My budget was growing higher and higher, and I thought that instead of compromising quality, I would just move my project to funding tier 3.
![2nd list iteration](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/dd375f65641b6b8f40520db66f2c4d06d94fa79a9338902c193a39bd0be95b6a.png)
 - It really opened up my eyes to the process of creating a new product; everything was relatively expensive, but the shipping was the real killer. I had to rely on Amazon HEAVILY in order to get past shipping costs.
 - After finagling with different products and shipping settings, I managed to maximize my quality vs budget ratio, and finally arrived at a list that I was happy with. I ran it through Claude, and it said that my list was good.
![Final part list](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/9f03670be4332630dfb4bc120f841b11ff51e6775dcf3058b0fcae8529f39bf5.png)

Hopefully, I can have my next session tomorrow. I'd like to start on the PCB and design.

tldr: Finding components is hard, and it takes a lot longer than I thought. I'm impressed by how cheap some factories can make items. I understand electronics pricing now. Starting over isn't a bad thing, and don't compromise on quality. Tomorrow is the start of design.

### 2026-10-11 – FINAL DAY LOCK IN

**13h**

FINAL DAY LOCK IN

Today I woke up with 1 thing in mind: get it finished. I woke up at 8:00 to get the project done.

**SCHEMATIC**
It was a real challenge learning how to use KiCad quickly, but with the help of Claude (who generated a guide) and YouTube, it turned out all right.

![PCD guide](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/cbecdd9cf43efa9566557b8c19e649985ef17e98f0f41b1566309bb1f089383d.png)
 - not much difficult here, if there was, it was definitely in how speeding up and slowing down motors really work.

I then reviewed the KiCad help guide for ~20 minutes.

![Kicad help](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/91e205959d8bfd501950097d973551ee428438aa13409a1a6935dd223fb2c2ea.png)

I replaced the controllers from my original BOM with this PCB so that more of my work on this project would be original.

![first SCH](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/33c4438cca597e6ddec573d7bdf92840a8e98fb2e72e8c336b2af6d65a00641b.png)
 - first half for the fan motor
 - values and ID were slightly confusing, but Claude explained it well, and it was easier than wiring manually

I next ran the ERC check before copying the design for the sand motor side.

![1stERC](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/faef075a05a2935aa3473c0263260138f5cd58695dba5f7178be75df5b844f62.png)
**ISSUES**
 - many of the problems were interconnected, so fixing 1 really fixed ~5, which was a great help
 - the rest of the problems were very minor and fixed easily, but some of them were persistently annoying (like blank labels being invisible)

I then copied the design and added the power section, easily replacing the S_ with F_ with CTRL+F search and replace.

![finished SCH](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/b3ff9fd2a34505d00cabf7f27178ea6c5ac514fad8b4f032dc23d6b98eaf2051.png)

With the guidance of YouTube and Claude, I learned what footprints were and how to add them, and then did so, which took me about 20 minutes as well

![finished footprints](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/292db9fac36e31b84fc10b2cc019d2422a08982743d96bce73b42318634f0b84.png)

All in all, this section probably took me about 5 hours.

**PCB**
I spent by far the most amount of time on the PCB. It was very confusing, and not much automation for the process.

![imported PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/36bf830d4902a6c2414899affacbaacd9523fa33616b2fede8031f51a40fcae9.png)
 - extremely confusing
 - How do I even begin to untangle this?

I first looked at other PCBs and references from other projects, and I finally arrived at a suitable position. It also took me a little bit to understand design constraints and tolerances.

![1st PCB!](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/01a29795ba89b802102b0c8a6c8e71718691baa848e5c85f4c766a1eab152955.png)

I then spent more time finalizing the design and getting the next steps of the process done, routing and silkscreening.

![finished routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/2fe33bacaa97f8b72fc90fb095920527881440790b396a9619be7fedef14cbef.png)
  - this part was pretty easy, it was just plug and go, but there were some challenges with constraints and tolerances that were resolved through some elbow grease

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/3fcd422754a70f489b11ee2b3730c632843a23e5870075d9c291453864179307.png)
 - I finalized the PCB with some more help from references, Claude, and YouTube. At this point, it started getting pretty convoluted, and I really needed some outside guidance, but I did figure it out eventually.

![minor issue1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/2746ea4d958ea26e21b0865857b3537c3197902f301e162bd437faeb19a7b7c2.png)
![minor issue2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/2bca0e706a4fdb65daf12abe1eca9b30e7122bd898befa23c4dfd4566d493769.png)
  - there were many issues that I thought were big problems but really turned out to be quite minor, which I spent a little bit of time on.

I then finished everything up, saved, and documented my work.

![FINALLY](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/8d35be406d8596ff705e27c0df29dc8bb1db1f43bdd893598d43b94e88377e31.png)

I then asked claude to commit and push all my local files to the main branch, and I was done!
